links.comparator_used: CDSS alerts with no pharmacist action (alerts reviewed by pharmacist but not acted on), i.e. natural course of alerts
links.outcome: Proportion of CDSS alerts resolved at day 1 and day 3
links.effect: Day 1: 36.1% vs 27.3% resolved (p<0.001); day 3: 62.4% vs 48.0% (p<0.001). Renal function category: 16.6% vs 10.6% (day 1) and 29.8% vs 19.4% (day 3), both p<0.001; other categories showed small non-significant positive effects.
links.tradeoff: Many alerts resolved without any pharmacist action (27% at day 1, 48% at day 3), suggesting many alerts may be low value or 'false positive' and could cause distraction/alert fatigue; retrospective observational design; broad definition of 'action' may overstate the pharmacist effect.
links.quote: In 4083 (51.6%) of the handled alerts, an action was performed by the pharmacist, resulting in 1297 (36.1% after excluding ‘unknown’) resolved alerts after day 1, while when the pharmacist did not perform an action, which was the case in 3824 alerts, 915 (27.3% after excluding ‘unknown’) alerts were resolved (36.1% vs 27.3%, p < 0.001).

design_hint: pharmacist review and action on CDSS alerts
